title: Max Sum Subarray of Size K
description: Given an array of numbers and an integer k, return the maximum sum of any contiguous subarray of length k.
whatShouldHappen: Compute the sum of the first window (first k elements).
Slide the window one step right each iteration.
Add the incoming element and subtract the outgoing element.
Track the maximum window sum seen and return it.
patternExplanation: Instead of recomputing each window sum from scratch (O(n·k)), reuse the previous sum by adding the incoming element and subtracting the outgoing one — O(n) total.

title: Longest Subarray with Sum ≤ K
description: Given an array of non-negative integers and a value k, return the length of the longest contiguous subarray whose sum is at most k.
whatShouldHappen: Use a left and right pointer both starting at 0.
Expand the window by advancing the right pointer and adding to the running sum.
If the sum exceeds k, shrink the window by advancing the left pointer and subtracting.
After each step, update the maximum window length seen.
patternExplanation: Expand with the right pointer and shrink with the left — the window size flexes to maintain a constraint, avoiding the need to restart from every possible left boundary.

title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
description: Given a string s, find the length of the longest substring without repeating characters using a dynamic sliding window.
whatShouldHappen: Maintain a map of character -> last seen index.
Expand the window with right pointer from 0 to s.length - 1.
If s[right] is already in the map and at/after left pointer, slide left to map.get(s[right]) + 1.
Update map with right index and record max window length.
patternExplanation: Expand right to consume characters; jump left forward past any duplicate index to keep window elements unique in O(n) time.

title: Find All Anagrams in a String
description: Given two strings s and p, return an array of all the start indices of p's anagrams in s. Both strings consist of lowercase English letters.
whatShouldHappen: Count character frequencies in p.
Maintain a sliding window of length p.length across string s.
Increment frequency for incoming character and decrement for outgoing character.
Whenever window frequency matches p frequency, record starting index.
patternExplanation: Keep a fixed window of size |p| and maintain rolling character counts, comparing them against target counts in O(26) per step.

title: Maximum Number of Vowels in a Substring of Given Length
description: Given a string s and an integer k, return the maximum number of vowel letters ('a', 'e', 'i', 'o', 'u') in any substring of s with length k.
whatShouldHappen: Initialize count of vowels in first window of size k.
Set maxCount = current count.
Slide the window by 1: if incoming char is vowel, increment; if outgoing char is vowel, decrement.
Update maxCount at each step and return it.
patternExplanation: Slide a fixed-size window across the string in O(n) time, adjusting only the delta of the newly entered and evicted characters.

title: Max Consecutive Ones with At Most K Flips
description: Given a binary array nums and an integer k, return the maximum number of consecutive 1's in the array if you can flip at most k 0's.
whatShouldHappen: Maintain a window [left, right] and a counter for zeros in window.
Iterate right pointer over nums: if nums[right] === 0, increment zeros.
If zeros > k, shrink window from left until zeros <= k.
Track max window size (right - left + 1) and return it.
patternExplanation: Expand right to consume numbers while shrinking left whenever the window constraint (zeros <= k) is violated in amortized O(n) time.

title: Subarray Product Less Than K
description: Given an array of integers nums and an integer k, return the number of contiguous subarrays where the product of all elements in the subarray is strictly less than k.
whatShouldHappen: If k <= 1, return 0 because array elements are positive.
Initialize prod = 1, left = 0, and total = 0.
For each right pointer, multiply prod by nums[right].
While prod >= k and left <= right, divide prod by nums[left] and increment left.
Add (right - left + 1) to total (each new valid window adds this many new subarrays ending at right).
patternExplanation: Every time right expands, exactly (right - left + 1) contiguous subarrays ending at right are valid and counted in O(n) total operations.
